I want to express my congratulations to Secretary Hegseth, the United States Army, and the entire stellar federal interagency — EPA Administrator Zeldin, FEMA Administrator Hamilton, HHS Secretary Kennedy, USDA Secretary Rollins, CDC Director Schwartz, ATF Director Cekada, NASA Administrator Isaacman, Energy Secretary Wright, and countless munitions, environmental, weather, and health experts across the federal government — for flawlessly executing the controlled demolition of the explosive materials improperly placed and stored by the Obama Administration in Iowa in 2009.

Every single extraordinary mitigation measure put into place far exceeded expectations, and the technical mastery of the army technicians in directing the controlled blast downward into the earth, while simultaneously activating and funneling all deployed multilayered suppression and monitoring measures, demonstrates that the U.S. Military’s engineering prowess is truly second to none. 

Not only did the military and civilian experts on the scene perform brilliantly under pressure, but they did so at personal risk to life and limb working in continuous proximity to a chemical compound determined by all experts inside and outside government to be at imminent risk of spontaneous unconstrained self-detonation (based on the advanced rate of desiccation, crystallization and the mechanical effects of plummeting temperatures on accelerating the decay). 

The 2009 storage decision placed Iowa at peril of a sudden, unsuppressed, unmonitored and unmitigated detonation of lead azide (in potentially adverse weather conditions and without warning). President Trump’s leadership team leapt into action and, through intricate planning and immense technical skill, not only saved Iowa and the surrounding states from such an uncontrolled detonation, but achieved a marvel of physical engineering and timing to seamlessly eliminate this threat to public health.

Many thanks as well to Governor Reynolds and Governor-elect Sand and all state and local officials for their cooperation and engagement.

A tremendous display of unity of effort, purpose and action led by President Trump.

posts.text:
Ice Cube CONFRONTS Bill Maher over his use of the N-word: “You might have Black friends, but that doesn't mean you can cross the line” and tells him why some jokes cross the line, even after an apology.

Ice Cube: Now, you got a lot of Black jokes. Sometimes you sound like a redneck trucker, you know, Bill.

Bill Maher: No, I don’t.

Ice Cube: Yes, you do.

Bill Maher: That I got to push back on.

Ice Cube: My thing is this, I’m cool with you. I like your show, to be honest. I just want to know: What made you think it was cool to say that?

Bill Maher: There was no thought put into it. Comedians, they react. It was wrong and I apologized. More than that, I can’t do.

Ice Cube: I accept your apology. But I still think we need to get to the root of the psyche. A lot of guys cross the line because they think they’re too familiar. They might have a Black girlfriend or some Black friends, and they think they can cross the line. And they can’t.

It’s a word that’s been used as a weapon against us by white people. And we’re not going to let that happen again by nobody.

When I hear my homie say it, it don’t feel like venom. When I hear a white person say it, it feels like that knife stabbing me, even if they don’t mean it.

And sometimes the jokes step on the political messages you’re trying to deliver. Some things just ain’t funny.

I haven't read this takedown of Taylor Swift yet and I have pretty neutral feelings about her but I will say I was completely shocked she never released a single photo of her wedding dress to her fans. She gave them absolutely nothing--no wedding pix, no wedding Instagram photo dump, literally nothing. Her IG was like it never happened. An event so huge it shut down Midtown, but on social media it was like it was On her Reddit fan page they were posting things cope like she's probably too busy, she's just private, etc.

After a 20 year career singing about her broken heart to the fans who made her a superstar, I thought they deserved to see a tiny glimpse of the big finale to that journey.

She gave them nothing. Except some new album re-releases to buy, and probably a wedding movie to rent later for $29.99.

I felt bad for the women who worship her. She didn't need to throw them her bouquet, but couldn't she throw them a bone?

posts.text:
RICARDO KAKÁ LES MANDA A DECIR A TODOS LOS HOMBRES QUE EL AMOR NO SE PUEDE FORZAR. 👏🙂

"Hice todo lo posible para salvar mi matrimonio, pero hay algo que aprendí: no puedes obligar a alguien a quedarse contigo si ya decidió irse. En 2015, mi esposa me dijo que ya no quería estar casada. Me aferré a la idea de luchar, de demostrarle que podíamos recuperar lo que teníamos. Leí un libro que proponía un reto de 40 días para reconquistar a tu pareja; lo hice dos veces. Regalos, cartas, sorpresas inesperadas… pero al final, ella solo repetía: 'No quiero más'. 

"Fue un golpe brutal. Como cristiano, el divorcio no estaba en mis planes. La Biblia dice que el matrimonio es para siempre, pero ¿Qué haces cuando la otra persona ya no quiere continuar? Luché hasta el final, hasta que entendí algo clave: el amor no se puede forzar. El amor es una elección diaria. Y si alguien deja de elegirte, debes aprender a dejar ir".

Consejos del balón de oro 🪙🥇

Scott Aaronson says he has heard repeated rumours that OpenAI, Anthropic, or both may have discovered a polynomial-time algorithm for integer factorisation

Ledger’s CTO says he is hearing similar rumours involving THREE major cryptographic foundations:

→ RSA FACTORISATION: A practical breakthrough could undermine RSA encryption and digital signatures used across banking, internet infrastructure and government systems

ELLIPTIC CURVE CRYPTOGRAPHY: A practical attack could compromise ECDSA and ECDH. Bitcoin relies on elliptic-curve signatures, meaning exposed public keys could become a serious target

RING-LWE: A breakthrough against this family of lattice-based problems could undermine important post-quantum cryptographic systems being developed to replace today’s vulnerable standards

THE BITCOIN ANGLE:
Bitcoin does not use RSA. It relies on elliptic-curve cryptography to secure ownership of funds

If the underlying elliptic-curve problem became practically solvable, attackers could potentially derive private keys from exposed public keys and steal BTC

SHA-256 mining would not automatically be broken by such a discovery

BUT THERE IS A MAJOR CAVEAT:
None of these cryptographic breakthroughs has been publicly demonstrated or independently verified

Ledger’s CTO says he remains skeptical that these primitives have been completely broken

The concern is that if a frontier AI lab actually discovered a practical attack, disclosing it responsibly without triggering a global security crisis could be extraordinarily difficult
